hints: Notice $\theta$ is measured from the dashed horizontal line up to $F$, so the horizontal side is adjacent to $\theta$.
Recall for hypotenuse $F$ that adjacent $= F\cos\theta$ and opposite $= F\sin\theta$.
Check the trig identity $\cos(90^\circ - \theta) = \sin\theta$ to see which vertical forms match $F\sin\theta$.
walkthrough: Draw the right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $F$, base along the horizontal and vertical side opposite $\theta$.
Use resolution: component adjacent to angle $= F \times \cos$ of the angle, component opposite angle $= F \times \sin$ of the angle.
Horizontal component is adjacent to $\theta$, so it is $F\cos\theta$.
Vertical component is opposite $\theta$, so it is $F\sin\theta$.
Apply $\cos(90^\circ - \theta) = \sin\theta$, so $F\cos(90^\circ - \theta)$ is another way to write $F\sin\theta$.
That pair $F\cos\theta$ and $F\cos(90^\circ - \theta)$ matches the table row. This is option A.

options.A: Horizontal is $F\cos\theta$ and $F\cos(90^\circ - \theta) = F\sin\theta$, which is the correct vertical opposite side.
options.B: Horizontal $F\cos\theta$ is correct, but $F\sin(90^\circ - \theta) = F\cos\theta$ equals the horizontal value, not the vertical value.
options.C: The components are swapped: $F\sin\theta$ is the vertical opposite side and $F\cos\theta$ is the horizontal adjacent side.
options.D: Horizontal $F\sin\theta$ is wrong, while vertical $F\cos(90^\circ - \theta) = F\sin\theta$ alone is correct.
